glossary.definition: An embedding is a way of converting a word, sentence, or image into a long list of numbers that captures its meaning, arranged so that similar concepts end up numerically close together. Imagine plotting every word in the dictionary on a giant map where "king" and "queen" end up as close neighbors, and "queen" and "bicycle" end up on opposite sides of the map. That numerical map is the mathematical backbone behind AI search, recommendations, and how models compare meaning rather than just exact spelling.

items.title: Microsoft brings AI inference closer to enterprise data with Windows Server 2028
items.summary: Microsoft is betting on a hybrid future where AI inferencing takes place where it makes the most sense. Which, logically, is where data already lives: On enterprise-controlled infrastructure. To that end, this week at Microsoft Ignite , the tech giant announced Windows Server 2028, its largest platform update since Windows Server 2025. ” It introduces new AI accelerators so enterprises can run inference on their own infrastructure, storage tools for accelerated data transfer, security controls to establish a “secure baseline from day one,” and simplified admin and management dashboards.

items.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit, rather than reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. The short answer is AI, but not in the way you might expect. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect.

items.title: Google Cloud brings AI agents to the supercomputing bottleneck
items.summary: High-performance computing, or HPC, is merging with artificial intelligence faster than many research teams can adapt. Compute capacity is hard to get, and workloads now run across clouds and on-premises clusters. The metric that matters is shifting from peak performance to time to discovery. That shift is on full display as supercomputing and AI converge at SC26 in Chicago.

items.title: Amidst fears of AI cyberattacks, Satya Nadella says lots of critical infrastructure is ‘unpatchable’
items.summary: The Microsoft CEO downplayed the recent Outlook outage while noting that AI was causing both opportunities and new challenges for securing much of the connected world. During his appearance at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella lamented the fact that a lot of America’s software systems — including those governing everyday hardware and transportation systems — suffer from unfixable software vulnerabilities that, in the age of AI-aided cyberattacks, are just waiting to be exploited. “Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable,” Nadella said. “I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else.

items.title: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
items.summary: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times . Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Google is trying to force Gemini on schools, and they’re not thrilled. ” Mamdani had recently announced a policy that barred 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom.

items.title: Does Nvidia Got This? Interim CEO Colette Kress Says It’s Got This
items.summary: WIRED is tallying up how many times Nvidia’s interim CEO has assured everyone that the company has everything under control. Nvidia is going through it. The chipmaker’s iconic leader just resigned due to an international scandal, its stock has taken a hit, and it’s in a precarious position as it tries to maintain its dominance in the AI era. Following Jensen Huang’s ouster, the company’s interim CEO and still-CFO, Colette Kress, has been tasked with stabilizing the deck.

items.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth new Gemini model in a month
items.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a new frontier model built for software development, knowledge work, and science. It handles text, images, video, audio, and PDFs with a context window of one million tokens. At $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, Neon is priced above previous Gemini 4 models. " The model is live today through the API at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, above Carbon and Argon's introductory rate of $2/$10 (doubling to $4/$20 on December 1 ) and twice the price of Hydrogen at $1.50/$7.50.

items.title: A new critical Java hole illustrates the enterprise IT visibility problem
items.summary: When cybersecurity research firm Calif published details Tuesday of a potentially major Java security flaw, dubbed Java4Shell, it described an unauthenticated attacker’s ability to read Java heap memory, steal private keys, tokens, and session secrets, and reach remote code execution (RCE). With Java being all-but-ubiquitous in today’s enterprise, coupled with the inability of CISOs to have visibility into every instance of it in their estate, this means that the bug could be a big problem for IT. Java, which has had its fair share of cybersecurity issues lately, is well-known for safely handling memory. That is why a Java bug affecting memory management is so dangerous.

items.title: The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere
items.summary: Like a nasty rash, AI seems to spread everywhere. Google crams AI Overviews down your throat even though it costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue. Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms. Go to the supermarket, and perhaps you’ll slip on a pool of melted ice cream congealing on the floor thanks to an AI-assisted cyberattack .

items.title: Network Rail Awards £133 Million Infrastructure Contract to Cognizant
items.summary: UK railway infrastructure operator Network Rail has selected Cognizant to manage its data centre infrastructure under a contract valued at £133.2 million (~$175 million). Moneycontrol first reported the contract award, based on a notice published on the UK government's procurement portal. The nearly seven-year engagement covers the management of Network Rail's data centre infrastructure. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), HCLTech, DXC Technology and Atos IT Services UK were the other bidders.

items.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
items.summary: " The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

items.title: Inspiring FOSS project Crosspoint Reader has lessons about tech, communities, and LLMs
items.summary: The Ubuntu Summit isn't all about Ubuntu, or even Linux. The second day opened with a talk from CrossPoint Reader project lead Justin Mitchell, with both good and bad news for all kinds of FOSS. The talk, EPUBs, ESP32s, and Everyone's A Developer Now, was all about a FOSS project that isn't Linux-based – because the devices it targets are much too small to run even the smallest, most cut-down distro. Recently, a new generation of roughly credit-card sized ebook readers has been thriving.
